lines: Duke Kahanamoku was born in 1890 in Honolulu, Hawaii.
He was a good swimmer and surfer from a young age.
As a swimmer, he went to the Olympics in Stockholm in 1912 and won a gold medal in the 100-meter freestyle.
He won medals in the 1920 and 1924 Olympics as well.
His swimming style was so smooth and fast that many people called him a “human fish.”
Kahanamoku also worked hard to make surfing popular.
He was one of the “Waikiki Beach Boys” who taught visitors how to surf in Hawaii.
In 1914, he even traveled to other countries to show surfing to new people.
Thanks to him, many people around the world became interested in surfing.
Kahanamoku is now called the “father of modern surfing.”
Today, a statue of him stands on Waikiki Beach, and people in Hawaii still respect him.
